newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TERRY FRANCONA TO MANAGE PHILLIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TERRY FRANCONA TO MANAGE PHILLIES.

text.p: The Philadelphia Phillies named Detroit Tigers third base coach Terry Francona their new manager Wednesday.
Francona, Phillies third base coach Larry Bowa and former Kansas City Royals manager Hal McRae were considered the leading candidates for the job. Francona received a two-year contract.
"After a long and exhaustive search, I've chosen Terry," said Phillies general manager Lee Thomas. "I did a lot of research on him and got overwhelmingly, positive responses from everyone."

The position became vacant when the Phillies fired Jim Fregosi on September 30th, one day after they finished with the worst record in the National League at 67-95. It was the Phillies' third straight losing season since they reached the World Series in 1993.

The 37-year-old Francona becomes the youngest manager in the major leagues. He spent last season as a third base coach for manager Buddy Bell in Detroit after four seasons managing in the Chicago White Sox farm system.
Francona played 10 years in the major leagues as an infielder with Montreal, the Chicago Cubs, Cincinnati, Cleveland and Milwaukee.
He was a lifetime .274 hitter in 708 career games. Francona's father, Tito, played 15 years in the major leagues.
